To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
We have developed a robust workflow for phospho-proteome analysis of pancreatic cancer tissue and identified many new candidate biomarkers and drug targets.

1) We have developed a workflow for global phospho-protein quantitation in pancreatic cancer tissue that is suitable for clinical use; 2) We found that the majority of proteins and phosphopeptides that are significantly differentially regulated in pancreatic cancer are new candidate markers; and 3) The data indicate that the molecular events likely contributing cancer are common to all cases, but the extent of their regulation varies between cases.

the proteome and phospho-proteome of pancreatic cancer tissue can be quantified and used to identify the common, as well as the case-specific, molecular events contributing to cancer, and to predict activity of signaling pathways, drug targets and potential biomarkers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a global phosphoproteomic workflow to determine the activity of signaling pathways, and drug targets in tissue from pancreatic cancer patients for clinical application.
the identification of biomarkers and drug targets for the early detection and treatment of pancreatic cancer.
the development of new tools to help unravel the molecular events that lead and propagate cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this study has provided the first detailed proteome and phosphoproteome of human pancreatic cancer and background tissue.
this is the most comprehensive study of its type to date.
the data presented is a significant step towards the goal of providing a more personalised treatment for cancer patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have established a workflow to quantify the proteome and phosphorylome of human pancreatic cancer tissue.
this is the first time the phospho-proteome and proteome of human pancreatic cancer tissue has been quantified in this manner.

we have demonstrated the power of LC-MS/ MS phospho-proteome analysis to provide critical information for the identification of the common and unique events likely contributing to pancreatic cancer in each case, and that this information may be used for the prediction of more bespoke therapy suitable to an individual case.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the phospho-proteome of pancreatic cancer tissue is highly dynamic and that the phosphorylation status of a number of proteins and drug targets is highly predictive of disease progression.

the use of a global phospho-MS/MS approach to determine protein phosphorylation status is a powerful tool that can be used to help identify new markers of pancreatic cancer, and to help predict the activity of drug targets in individual cases.
LC-MS/ MS phospho-proteome analysis is an essential technology in the quest for personalized medicine for pancreatic cancer and likely other cancers.
